records.title: EU Preparedness Union Strategy: Non-legislative strategy adopted in 2025
records.claim: The European Commission adopted the Preparedness Union Strategy on March 26, 2025. Its official implementation tracker lists it as an adopted non-legislative item.
records.scope: Adoption of the EU-level strategy; confirms only the nature and adoption date of this strategy document.

sources.title: Security and defence implementation tracker
sources.locator: Non-legislative items > Adopted: EU preparedness union strategy entry dated March 26, 2025, and the section introduction
sources.supports: Supports the Commission adoption and date of this non-legislative strategy; does not establish implementation of subsequent actions.

sources.publisher: European Commission and High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy
sources.title: Joint Communication on the European Preparedness Union Strategy (JOIN(2025) 130 final)
sources.locator: Cover (PDF page 1): institutions, document identifier and Brussels, 26.3.2025
sources.supports: Confirms the identity and date of the original Joint Communication.

records.verification_note: An AI agent read the listed original official sources during this review and checked each cited location. verified means the evidence supports this precise claim; it does not mean human certification or independent field verification.
limitations: adopted describes only adoption of the non-legislative strategy document. It does not establish new legal obligations for households or completion of all 30 key actions.
Member-state laws and progress on subsequent measures were not reviewed for this record; effective_at remains null.

change_history.summary: Record created from official original sources read during this review. Review method: AI agent source review; independent human review remains pending.

records.title: EU 72-hour self-sufficiency guidelines: Planned action in the 2025 strategy
records.claim: Key action 14 of the March 26, 2025 strategy states that the Commission will propose guidelines for member states to achieve population self-sufficiency for at least 72 hours. The annex gives 2026 as the indicative year for developing the guidelines.
records.scope: Describes only the guideline-development plan when the 2025 strategy was published. It does not determine whether separate guidelines had been issued or countries had legislated by the review date.

sources.publisher: European Commission and High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy
sources.title: Joint Communication on the European Preparedness Union Strategy (JOIN(2025) 130 final)
sources.locator: Section 3, Population Preparedness; printed page 10 (PDF page 11), key action 14 and its first paragraph
sources.supports: Supports the plan to propose guidelines for at least 72 hours of self-sufficiency to member states. This describes a future action, not a law requiring household stockpiles.

sources.publisher: European Commission and High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy
sources.title: Action Plan annex to the European Preparedness Union Strategy
sources.locator: Cover; printed page 1 describes the indicative timeline; printed page 3 (PDF page 4), row 28
sources.supports: The annex gives 2026 as the indicative year for developing 72-hour self-sufficiency guidelines, without a month, day or evidence of completion.

records.verification_note: An AI agent read the listed original official sources during this review and checked each cited location. verified means the evidence supports this precise claim; it does not mean human certification or independent field verification.
limitations: announced describes the future guideline-development plan in the original text. It does not claim that a draft has been proposed, entered into force or been completed.
2026 is only an indicative year. Current date fields require a complete date, so target_at is null and must not be filled with an invented December 31 date.
Guideline progress after the 2025 document and member-state requirements were not reviewed. This record does not establish a complete account of current national or household obligations.

change_history.summary: Organized from the existing README as a pending research lead; no factual verification was performed.
Split eu-household-preparedness-lead into this guideline-plan record and a separate strategy-adoption record. Removed the broad lead while preserving its history.

records.title: rescEU energy reserve: Official report of generator deployments to Ukraine
records.claim: The European Commission rescEU page reports that rescEU has deployed thousands of generators to Ukraine to help hospitals and other critical infrastructure maintain essential services.
records.scope: Actual rescEU energy-reserve deployments to Ukraine, according to the official programme page accessed on September 20, 2026.

sources.publisher: European Commission Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations (DG ECHO)
sources.title: Official rescEU programme description
sources.locator: rescEU at a glance > Energy, final paragraph (beginning with In response)
sources.supports: Supports the official report of thousands of generators deployed and their purpose. It provides neither an itemized inventory for recalculation nor a deployment start date.

records.verification_note: An AI agent read the listed original official sources during this review and checked each cited location. verified means the evidence supports this precise claim; it does not mean human certification or independent field verification.
limitations: This is source review of the programme authority's public statement, not an independent audit. Itemized delivery records and precise quantities were not verified.

The page is a changing programme description. Its footer update date of August 11, 2026 cannot replace unknown original-publication, deployment or completion dates; the relevant date fields remain null.

implementing indicates only evidence of energy-reserve implementation, not completion of all rescEU capabilities. Hosting-country counts with unclear definitions in different sections of the same page were not used.
